frames.review_note: Minor only: the topknot sits high on the crown but much of his curly hair falls loose around the neck, and there is faint warm shading on the jaw that reads as skin texture, not a beard. The moustache, clean chin, gold ear stud, grey temples, silver chain, ivory conch-knife at the waist and the scar on the inner LEFT forearm all match. The room has lime-washed laterite walls, a dark timber ceiling, a closed shutter, a woven mat, a low table with string-bound palm-leaf bundles and a single open-wick lamp. There is no writing on the leaves. Hands are sound. A large clear plaster wall in the upper left has room for both long captions.

Acceptable, with minor faults. Nagoji has a high topknot over loose curls, a thick curled moustache and a flush gold ear stud, but light stipple shading on his chin and jaw could read as faint stubble when zoomed in, and no silver chain, conch knife or grey at the temples shows in this wide shot. Revathi's grey is a visible streak at the temple rather than a few threads. The drums are barrel-shaped rather than true chenda. A tiny blue glint sits at the top of the roof. Beat delivered: dusk, a tiled Kerala roof, a tall brass lamp-pillar, women in white carrying brass lamps, drummers, Nagoji at the edge of the crowd and Revathi across the courtyard by the offering stones, with no tali. There is clear dusk sky at top centre-right (about x 0.47 to 0.80, y 0 to 0.25) for both captions.

Acceptable. Two right hands meet over prasadam on a banana leaf on a brass plate, and the fingertips touch: his has a cream gold-striped shoulder cloth at the wrist and no brand, hers has gold bangles and an indigo-and-gold sari. The thumb placement reads correctly for both right hands, and no tali or text is visible. Minor: the soft-focus background (temple, lamp-pillar, procession, tank) and the foreground lamp and bowls are rendered more painterly and photographic than the inked style of the neighbouring panels, while the hands themselves are inked. Both hands dip into the rice rather than just reaching. The medium caption fits across the top band over the blurred roof, palms and sky (about y 0 to 0.12).

Acceptable. Nagoji has a high topknot, clean chin, thick curled moustache, flush gold ear stud, silver chain of office and a cream mundu with shoulder cloth. Revathi has an indigo-and-gold sari, a jasmine braid, a flat-coin necklace, gold armlets, a sandalwood line, subtle grey threads and no tali. They stand side by side at dusk, both watching the lamp procession to the right without looking at each other, with lamplight on both faces, in the same temple as 1.2. Minor: Nagoji's grey is a little heavier than 'first grey at the temples', and the conch knife is out of frame below. The four short balloons fit over the tiled roof at top left above Revathi (about x 0.02 to 0.40, y 0.01 to 0.16) and the night sky and palms at top right (about x 0.65 to 0.85, y 0.01 to 0.22).

Both figures are tiny, as the script asks, so facial details cannot be checked at this scale. The small Nagoji wears white with a topknot. Revathi is in an indigo sari with a gold border and jasmine in her braid, and her tali is not visible. They walk toward each other from opposite ends of the tank path. The scene has two hawks circling, a morning sky, a tiled Kerala temple roof, a brass lamp-pillar, coconut palms and a stepped tank. There is no text. The upper half is open sky, with ample room for both captions.

Minor only: Revathi is shown already mounted rather than standing beside her horse (still reads as 'she has stopped' and sets up 2.3 riding away); her sandalwood hairline line and grey threads are not distinct at this size. Nagoji matches: topknot, grey temples, thick curled moustache, clean chin, small flush gold stud, chain of office, ivory conch knife at waist. No tali on Revathi. Wide dusk sky across the upper middle and right gives ample room for four balloons.

Clean. Revathi is unsmiling and stern, with the indigo-and-gold sari, jasmine braid, flat-coin necklace, gold armlets, sandalwood line, a few grey threads and no tali. She is mounted, with the same white-turbaned spear escort and dusk village as 2.1 and 2.3. The upper-right dusk sky is clear enough for both balloons; a few spear tips reach into it, which does no harm.

Minor. The script asks for Nagoji small at the village edge, but he is a large over-the-shoulder figure in the left foreground. The beat (she rides off with her escort, he is left watching among the last lamps) still reads. Because he is seen from behind, the chain of office and knife are not visible. Revathi's head is in profile, looking ahead and to the side, not back at him. Otherwise he matches the bible: topknot, grey at the temples, moustache, clean chin, gold stud, mundu and shoulder cloth. The escort, horses and dusk match 2.1 and 2.2. A large clear sky across the top fits both captions.

Minor: faint stubble texture on Nagoji's jaw, still reads clean-shaven. Otherwise clean: jackfruit tree, laterite house and kalari weapon rack behind, Padmini with black coiled hair threaded grey, cream gold-bordered drape, stick, fingers on the green cloth as Nagoji takes it with sound hands; Nagoji with topknot, grey temples, curled moustache, flush gold stud, chain and conch-marked ivory knife. Light sky between the roof and the tree (upper middle) holds the two short balloons.

Minor. This is a medium close-up with Nagoji's face looking down, not the tight hands-only insert in the script. The cloth is draped over his hands rather than spread open across his palms. The top of his head is cropped, so the topknot cannot be confirmed, though the swept-back hair and grey strands are consistent with 2.3. What works: the face matches (moustache, clean chin, small gold stud), the embroidery is an abstract vine with no letter-like marks, and the jackfruit tree and kalari yard match 2.4. Plain green cloth to the right of the vine (about x 0.80-0.97, y 0.60-0.95) can take the stitched caption. The upper-right foliage and tree area can take the two short captions without covering the face or hands.

Minor: the ivory-handled conch knife is not visible at his waist (could be on the hidden side under the draped cloth); he wears leather riding boots with the mundu. Otherwise clean: topknot, grey temples, curled moustache, clean chin, small gold stud, silver chain of office, Kayal correct bay with black points, musket-armed retainers at a timber gatehouse in laterite walls, children in the courtyard, pale moon over palms. Captions fit in the upper-left sky/palms and the sky right of Nagoji's head.

Minor issue: Revathi looks toward frame right, while 3.3 and 3.5 put Nagoji on the left looking right. The shot/reverse-shot does not quite line up, but this is a staging nicety, not a failure. Everything else matches: indigo and gold sari, jasmine braid, flat-coin necklace, gold armlets, sandalwood line, a few grey threads at the temple, no tali. The verandah, sunken kalari with boys and watching sisters, and women pounding grain are all there in late-afternoon light. No painted text. The hands are clasped and sound. Lettering space: open sky upper right (x 0.55 to 1.0, y 0 to 0.13) plus the plain roof tiles below it.

Minor issue: the grey at his temple is a little heavier than 'first grey', but it matches 3.5. Everything else matches: dry, arms-folded pose, Kerala topknot, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, tiny flush gold stud, silver chain of office, ivory conch-marked knife at his waist (page 3, correct), cream mundu and shoulder cloth. Same verandah, courtyard and light as 3.2. No text in the art; the medallion carries a design, not letters. Lettering space: open sky upper right (x 0.5 to 0.9, y 0.02 to 0.18).

The expression reads more as a knitted-brow frown with pressed lips than a mouth twitching against a smile, so the humour depends on the line. Otherwise clean: same few grey threads, sandalwood line, flat-coin necklace, no tali, jhumkas, jasmine braid, armlets, same verandah and light. The short balloon fits in the open sky at the upper right.

Three minor issues. (1) Nagoji's ear ornament is a tiny gold ball that sits a hair below the lobe rather than perfectly flush; at reading size (about 8 px) it reads as a small stud. (2) Revathi's grey threads do not show in this small side view. (3) Nagoji's topknot sits near the top edge (head at y 0.03 to 0.23), above the requested middle band. The beat itself is there: Nagoji walks the verandah; Revathi stops at the end pillar, hand on it, head turned to face him. Around them: a bangled woman with a pestle, boys sparring in the kalari, girls watching, hanging brass lamps with open wicks, low warm light. Nagoji has topknot, curled moustache, clean chin, chain and knife; Revathi has no tali, coin necklace, jasmine braid and sandalwood line. Hands are sound. No painted text. The setting matches 3.2 and 3.3. No lettering in this panel.

Minor only. A thin red line shows in her hair parting, which reads like sindoor on a widow; the few grey threads seen in 3.5 are not visible; her neck shows the flat-coin necklace with no tali, which is correct. She stands formally against the verandah pillar in low late-afternoon light, with the kalari pit and pounding women across the courtyard. Hands are clean. The clear sky in the upper right takes the long balloon, and the ceiling or the floor in the lower middle can take the short one.

Minor only. The brand and white scar show on the outer face of his crossed LEFT forearm rather than the inner side, but it is the correct arm. The brass standing lamps are lit in daylight. Nagoji matches the Ananthan Pillai sheet and the ch20 row: curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, a flush gold stud, a topknot with grey temples, the silver chain and the ivory conch knife at his waist. The verandah, kalari pit and grain-pounding women match the setting. There is clear sky at the upper right for his balloon.

Minor only. The few grey threads from 3.5 are not visible. Her necklace is the round-bead style from her sheet rather than flat coins, with no tali. The ghost of a smile reads well, and the setting, light and costume match 4.1. Hands are sound. The two short balloons can sit on the dark ceiling to the right of her head, on the pale wall at upper left, or on the floor in the lower middle.

Acceptable, with one small continuity flaw worth a retouch. The brand on Nagoji's inner left forearm is drawn as a neat dark ring with a faint cross-like mark inside. The bible calls for a pale, blurred, puckered patch that is not a cross; it is tiny at reading size. The conch knife at his waist is hidden under the shoulder-cloth drape. A faint thread line runs below Revathi's bead necklace, with no pendant. Everything else is right. Nagoji has his topknot, grey temples, curled moustache, clean chin, gold stud, silver chain and bare chest with a cream mundu and shoulder cloth, matching 3.5. Revathi steps toward him and searches his face, with the pillar and empty floor between them. Hands are sound. Sky and roof at upper left and between the pillar and Nagoji leave room for both short balloons.

Minor only. Revathi's grey threading is a little more visible than 'a few threads'. Lettering space is moderate: a short balloon fits in the upper-left sky. The long balloon fits in the sky and dust plume between the rider and her hair, or in the pale dust at the lower left, as long as both stay clear of the rider and her face. She matches her sheet with no tali: indigo-and-gold sari, jasmine braid, flat-coin necklace, gold armlets, jhumkas and the sandalwood line. Nagoji appears only as the small rider seen from behind, with a topknot and white shoulder cloth, on a bay with a black mane, going away up a dust road in brown Deccan hills. The memory bleeds in as a stain, as the script asks. The verandah matches panel 4.2.

Acceptable, with three small flaws. 1) Revathi has a thin red sindoor streak in her hair parting (around x 0.27, y 0.14). It is a marriage mark she should not wear before the wedding, and it is absent in panels 2 and 3, so a small paint-out is worth doing. 2) Nagoji has faint stubble shading along the jaw. 3) The conch knife is hidden under his shoulder-cloth drape. Otherwise on model: Nagoji has a topknot, grey temples, a curled moustache, a flush gold stud and the silver chain. Revathi has the indigo sari, jasmine braid, armlets and coin necklace, with no tali. The verandah, the open council-room door, the empty mats, the carved seat and the guard with the musket all match. The balloons can go on the plain wall above Revathi and on the wall and door frame to the right of Nagoji's head.

Clean. Revathi is on model: long jasmine braid, bell earrings, coin necklace, armlets, sandalwood line, no tali, no sindoor. Her chin is lifted as she passes the open council-room door, the mats lie empty and the turbaned guard holds his musket upright. The carved seat reads a little like a settee but is low and wooden. The caption fits top-left over the sky and pillars. The long balloon fits over the council-room ceiling and upper lattice, or over the floor between the mat rows.

Minor: framed as a head-and-shoulders close-up rather than truly tight on the eyes, but the lattice light falls across her eyes as scripted. Revathi is on model, with a visible grey thread, the jasmine braid and no tali. She is inside the council room, between panel 2 (passing the door) and panel 5 (at the seat), and a distant guard stands in the doorway. Both balloons fit on the plain lit wall at the top right (about x 0.62 to 0.85, y 0 to 0.25).

Clean pick. Nagoji matches the Ananthan Pillai sheet and the ch20 row: topknot high on the crown, grey at the temples, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold stud, silver chain, white mundu and shoulder cloth, and the ivory conch knife at his waist. His left hand rests flat on the door frame and the anatomy is sound. He has the small smile the script asks for. The brand on the inner left forearm faces away, which is correct. The white-turbaned guard with a musket and the empty mats and carved seat match panels 5.1 to 5.3. The plain gold wall at upper right, above the lattice, is clear space for Nagoji's balloon. Minor: the topknot is a loose curly bun rather than a tight knot.

Acceptable, with small continuity flaws. The beat reads correctly: the shot is from behind Revathi, her hand rests on the back of the low carved seat at the head of the empty mats, and Nagoji stands small in the bright doorway. Revathi matches her sheet: indigo and gold sari, jasmine braid, gold armlet and bangles, gold earring, and no tali visible. At small scale Nagoji still shows his topknot, curled moustache, clean chin, ear stud, silver chain and mundu with shoulder cloth; his knife is not clearly readable. Flaws: (1) The door guard wears a red turban and a sleeved white tunic, where panels 5.2 and 5.4 show a bare-chested guard in a white turban. This is a background costume mismatch only. (2) Revathi is fully lit rather than the dark silhouette the script asks for. Her face is turned away, so her listed tail points to the right side of her head, toward the doorway. Balloon space: the upper-left lattice above and left of her head is mid-detail but covers nothing important, and the narrow plain wall between her head and the left door leaf can also take a balloon. Keep balloons off Nagoji in the doorway and off the guard.

Minor: at this scale Revathi's sandalwood hairline line and grey threads are not visible (bindi only); the verandah hanging lamps are caged brass lanterns, not glass, so allowed. The only open space for her balloon is the roof tiles and violet sky across the top centre and right, which is enough for a medium balloon. No tali, every beat present (grandmothers on platform, women at the grain, girl lighting a tall brass lamp, kalari, child on a hip).

Minor: Nagoji's ivory-handled knife is not visible (his clasped hands and the mundu folds cover his waist). Otherwise clean. He has the topknot, grey temples, a clean chin, a small flush gold stud, a silver chain and the mundu with shoulder cloth. Revathi has the sandalwood line, grey threads, coin necklace, armlets and jasmine, and no tali. The two balloons fit in the roof and sky band at the top centre and right, above both faces.

Clean. Revathi matches the sheet and bible row: indigo sari with gold zari, jasmine braid, flat-coin necklace, gold armlets, sandalwood line at the hairline, no tali. Close, lamplit, troubled expression; courtyard at lamp-lighting with violet sky. Grey threads barely visible (minor). The long balloon fits in the clear violet sky at upper right, above the roofs.

Acceptable. Nagoji sits on the laterite steps looking down at the stone, hands clasped (anatomy sound). He has the thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, tiny flush gold ear stud, tied-up topknot with grey temples, ivory conch-marked knife at his waist and white mundu with shoulder cloth. Minor: his silver chain is drawn as a thin chain with no medallion. The background courtyard shows lamp-lighting, grandmothers, grain and a child on a hip. The caption fits in the clear sky across the top centre.

Acceptable. Like panel 4, Nagoji sits on the same steps in the same costume, now looking up and to the right toward the off-panel Revathi. He has the moustache, clean-shaven chin, flush gold stud, topknot with grey temples and the conch knife. Hands are sound. Minor: his chain is thin with no medallion (consistent with panel 4), and the face sits a little above the middle half. Two medium balloons fit in the violet sky and over the low treeline across the top, from x 0.40 to 0.85.

Minor only. The brand on his inner left forearm is not visible because his arms are crossed on the rail, which is acceptable. Kayal's lower legs are cropped by the frame. Everything else matches: topknot, grey temples, curled moustache, clean chin, gold stud, silver chain, ivory knife, Kayal with no white markings, hanging brass lamp with open wicks, and dusk sky upper left for the balloons.
Clean against sheets, bible row and script beat.

Acceptable, with one small continuity flaw worth a retouch. Seen at full zoom, the brand on the inner LEFT forearm is a pale patch made of small rings with a few radiating lines, a bit like a beetle. It is not letters, a cross or a crescent, and at reading size it is only a faint pale smudge. The long white scar starts near the elbow and runs onto the inner upper arm, not from the wrist toward the elbow. Everything else matches. Kayal is a bay with a black mane and black lower legs and no white markings, in a leather headstall with brass buckles and a rope lead. She pushes her muzzle into his cupped empty palms. Nagoji is bare-chested in a cream mundu and shoulder cloth, with a topknot, grey temples, thick curled moustache, clean chin, tiny gold ear stud, silver chain and the ivory conch knife at his waist. The stable, laterite wall, hanging brass lamp with open wicks and dusk sky match 7.1 and 7.2. The hands are sound and there is no painted text. Lettering: one balloon in the dusk sky right of his head (x 0.80 to 0.98, y 0.08 to 0.32), the other over the roof beams at upper left (x 0.03 to 0.38, y 0.02 to 0.18), clear of the lamp, his face and the hands.

Acceptable. Minor only: Nagoji's jaw has a faint skin texture that disappears at reading size and does not read as a beard. Revathi's front hair is curlier than in 7.2, but the long jasmine braid falls down the front of her sari as it does there. The beat reads clearly. Revathi smiles genuinely at Nagoji, chin on her hand, both leaning on the rail. Two small nieces run past and bicker at right, one clutching a small brass object. Nagoji has his topknot, grey temples, thick curled moustache, clean chin, tiny flush gold ear stud, silver chain, bare chest with the cream shoulder cloth and the ivory conch knife at his waist, as in 7.1 and 7.3. Revathi wears the indigo-and-gold sari, the long flat-coin necklace and no second chain or tali, with jhumkas, gold armlets and bangles, the sandalwood line and grey threads. Kayal has no white markings and wears the leather headstall with brass buckles. The stable, lamp and dusk light match the page, the hands are sound and there is no painted text. Lettering: both Revathi balloons go in the dusk sky at upper right (x 0.70 to 0.98, y 0.0 to 0.28), clear of the lamp, her head and the children, with tails down to her mouth.

Minor only. The child pulls Nagoji leftward, away from the kalari pit on the right, instead of toward it. The edges are crisp rather than soft and dissolving. Revathi wears an extra long gold chain, which is harmless in an imagined future. Otherwise the beat reads clearly: bare feet on the courtyard stones, a fruit-sticky child tugging his hand, and Revathi behind with one finger raised, scolding. Nagoji matches the sheet (topknot, curled moustache, clean chin, gold stud, chain, no weapons). The sky and plain cream wall upper right are clear for both captions.

Acceptable. The r1 correction landed: Nagoji now has a Kerala topknot, grey at the temples, a silver chain on his bare chest and the ivory conch-knife at his waist, with a thick curled moustache, a clean chin and a flush gold stud. He is unsteady, gripping the carved pillar, and Revathi holds his left forearm under the beam, with the full moon over the courtyard. Revathi has her indigo sari, flat-coin necklace, armlets, sandalwood line, jasmine braid, a few grey threads and no tali. Hands are sound and there is no painted text. Minor points: the topknot is a loose bun with long curls falling, the chain has no pendant, and Revathi's grey streak is a little strong. Lettering: put both balloons in the open sky at top right, between the eave and the moon (about x 0.62 to 0.98, y 0.02 to 0.25). Revathi's medium balloon can drop onto the plain roof tiles at right (about x 0.75 to 1.0, y 0.27 to 0.45). Keep them clear of both faces.

Acceptable. Minor points: Revathi's sandalwood line at the hairline is faint (a red bindi reads more strongly), and Padmini's grey is a little heavier than 'threading'. The top of the frame is jackfruit foliage, so Revathi's off-panel balloon should sit top right over the sky and leaves (about x 0.82 to 0.98, y 0.02 to 0.22) or top centre over the foliage, clear of both faces and Padmini's pointing hand. The tail goes to the top edge because the speaker is the present-day Revathi, outside the inset.

Acceptable, with continuity notes. The r1 fix landed: Nagoji has his hair gathered up at the crown, grey temples, the silver chain, the conch-knife at his waist, a curled moustache, a clean chin and the gold stud. He is laughing with his head back, and Revathi turns to him, startled. The setting is the moonlit verandah. Hands are sound and there is no painted text. Three things are off. His mundu and shoulder cloth have a gold kasavu border, while panels 1, 4 and 5 on this page show plain cream; this is allowed before the wedding but does not match the neighbouring panels. Revathi shows no visible grey threads, though the chapter bible asks for the same few grey threads all chapter. Both sit on the ledge, while panels 1 and 4 have them standing; this is carried over from the accepted r1 composition. Lettering: open dark sky across the top (about x 0.32 to 0.98, y 0.06 to 0.25, with the moon at x 0.86, y 0.06). Put Nagoji's short balloon top-left of centre and Revathi's long one top right, above her head.

Acceptable. The r1 red sash is gone: Nagoji is in a plain cream mundu and shoulder cloth, which matches panels 1 and 5. He has his topknot, grey temples, the silver chain, the ivory conch-knife at his waist, a curled moustache, a clean chin and the gold stud. He looks down at Revathi, serious, and the two stand close under the carved beam with the moon behind. Revathi has her sari, flat-coin necklace, armlets, sandalwood line, a few grey threads, a jasmine braid and clasped hands, and no tali. Hands are sound and there is no painted text. Note: the frame is portrait (1024 x 1536). Lettering: open moonlit sky at upper right (about x 0.45 to 0.98, y 0.08 to 0.27). Put Nagoji's long balloon above and right of his head, and Revathi's medium balloon below it, over the sky or the plain roof tiles (about x 0.5 to 1.0, y 0.27 to 0.33). Keep her balloon above her face.

Acceptable and the strongest Nagoji on the page: Kerala topknot, grey temples, silver chain of office, curled moustache and gold stud. Both faces are in profile under the carved beam with the moon behind, in a wide 3:1 strip. Revathi has her flat-coin necklace, a few grey threads, the sandalwood line, a jasmine braid and no tali. Minor: light ink hatching on Nagoji's jaw reads as faint stubble, and the knife at his waist is out of frame. The balloon fits in the open sky between the eave and the moon (about x 0.50 to 0.70, y 0.03 to 0.25).

Minor: Revathi reads a little younger here than in 9.2, and her few grey threads are very faint. Otherwise she matches the sheet: indigo and gold sari, jasmine braid, flat-coin necklace, gold armlets, sandalwood line at the hairline, and no tali. The setting is the moonlit verandah with brass lamps. Her hands are sound. The night sky in the upper right is clear for both balloons. Nagoji is off-panel, so his tail goes to the right edge.

Only v02 is listed as a candidate. It is clean. Nagoji matches the sheet and the ch20 row: a high topknot, grey at the temples, a thick curled moustache, a clean chin, a small flush gold stud, the silver chain, a cream mundu with shoulder cloth, and the ivory conch-handled knife at his waist. He leans with his arms crossed, half-smirking, which shows him trying not to grin. Revathi matches her sheet: indigo and gold sari, jasmine braid, gold bead necklace, armlets, and a sandalwood line at the hairline. She counts points off on her fingers. The setting is the same moonlit verandah as 9.1. One very minor point: a thin gold chain shows under her necklace, but it has no pendant, so it does not read as a tali. The open moonlit sky in the top centre, plus the beam area at upper left, gives room for all three balloons without covering a face or hand. There is no painted text.

Minor: Nagoji's silver chain hangs at his waist beside the knife instead of at his neck, and his mundu has a red-striped border. Both are acceptable in a tight insert. The hands are anatomically sound: his left hand and her right hand brush and lightly link. The conch-marked ivory knife is clearly at his waist, and her bangle, armlet and flat-coin necklace are correct. The moonlit verandah matches 9.1 and 9.2. The captions can sit over the sky between the figures and the plain mundu cloth in the upper left.

Clean. The wide wedding-morning courtyard shows the beat: women stringing jasmine garlands, a man polishing brass vessels, a white-haired elder at the lamps, and chenda drummers tuning under the eaves. There are no courtiers and no text. The open sky band along the top centre is fairly shallow for one long and one medium caption, but the captions can extend over the palm tops and roof tiles without covering any face or action.

Minor issues. Dhanaji's quilted sleeves are pushed up to mid-forearm, as on his sheet, not down to the wrist. He is still in the saddle, leaning to dismount, rather than clearly swinging down. The mark on Nagoji's left forearm is drawn as thin pale crossing lines, not a puckered patch, but it is small and not bloody. Otherwise both men are on model. Dhanaji has the white pagdi, short black beard, indigo quilted tunic, leather sword belt, talwar, boots and no sash, and he rides a dusty brown horse. Nagoji has the high topknot, grey temples, curled moustache, clean chin, small gold ear stud, silver chain, bare chest with shoulder cloth and mundu, and the ivory knife at his waist. The gate setting matches the script: laterite walls, a tiled gatehouse and musket-armed retainers. The sky in the upper left is clear for the caption.

Minor: Nagoji's silver chain of office is missing here (he wears it in 10.2 and 10.3). Dhanaji looks at Nagoji, not past his shoulder at the garlands. The two men clasp hands rather than forearms. Otherwise clean: both men laughing in the garlanded courtyard, the ivory conch knife at Nagoji's waist, Nagoji with topknot, grey temples, thick moustache, clean chin and gold stud, Dhanaji with white pagdi, short beard and indigo quilted tunic. Sky and roof at the upper left and top centre leave room for the four balloons.

Minor: the knife at Nagoji's waist has a curved ivory hilt that differs a little from the straight conch knife in 10.1 and 10.3. A small reddish scar mark sits on the outer left forearm instead of the inner. Dhanaji's boot is turned out but not clearly scuffing. The beat reads clearly: Dhanaji's grin is gone and he looks at the floor in riding boots, while Nagoji watches him with arms crossed, chain of office on and knife at his waist. Sky and roof between and above the heads take Dhanaji's two balloons.

Framed as a medium two-shot with both faces, not a tight hands-only inset. Dhanaji's palm is open, receiving the knife, while his other hand grips his own wrist; his fingers do not push back, though his frown carries the refusal. Everything else is correct: Nagoji's RIGHT hand (bare, hairy forearm, no brand) presses the knife into a palm that comes from an indigo sleeve; the knife has a straight narrow blade, ivory handle, gold guard and pommel and a gold conch near the hilt; his waist is empty; the chain of office is on. Open sky at the top centre between the heads takes both balloons.

v02 is the only listed candidate and it is acceptable. Nagoji matches the sheet and the ch20 @10.3- row: topknot with grey temples, thick curled moustache, clean chin, small flush gold ear stud, silver chain, white mundu and shoulder cloth, and no knife at his waist.
